We say: he sat communing with his Lord, complaining to Him of the harshness of these people and asking Him for support.

Many of the people of Makkah travel this journey from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis, and a rational proof can be established through it for one who does not believe in it.

Therefore, when his people denied him and said: "Do you claim that you were taken to Bayt al-Maqdis in a single night, while we travel to it for a month on the backs of camels?" Then they asked the Messenger of Allah to describe Bayt al-Maqdis to them and to give them signs on the road. Had they been certain of this journey, they would not have asked the Messenger of Allah that.

So they wanted to make the Messenger of Allah incapable. But Allah strengthened His Messenger and displayed before him a detailed image of Bayt al-Maqdis, so he began describing it to them. Then he informed them about the caravan that belonged to them on the trade route, that it was at such-and-such a place, and that it contained such-and-such. When their trading caravans arrived, they found it as the Messenger of Allah had said.

So: it was possible to establish proof of his truthfulness (ﷺ) in the journey of the Isra' to be a prelude to the Mi'raj, which is a heavenly journey that no one witnesses, and no rational proof can be established for it. But He who breached the cosmic laws for Muhammad in the Isra' can breach the laws for him in the Mi'raj.

So: He made the unseen for which a proof is established a prelude to the unseen for which there is no proof.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Except with truth…﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 3]. He means: I did not create (the heavens and the earth) in vain; rather I created them with a precise, firm order that does not change. We have said that "al-haqq" (truth) is the thing that is established and does not change. Likewise, I created them for a purpose. So look at the sky, for example: Allah created it without pillars.

It has been so since Allah created it, and it will remain so until the Hour arrives, in this stability, this firmness, and this truth with which it was created.

Likewise, the sun is the sun. It has not needed maintenance or spare parts, and no malfunction or defect has befallen it. Why? Because it was created with truth and with a justice that never changes, since it was built from its foundation upon wisdom. Had this universe been built from its inception on other than wisdom, it would have been struck by defect and disorder.

So: Allah created the heavens and the earth from the beginning upon truth, a truth that is demanded, which no falsehood preceded and no other creation preceded that was later modified. Rather, it has been so from its first origin, as we previously said in His saying, Exalted is He, when He addresses the enemies of Islam, so He said: ﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest…﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40].

The first is "made" (ja'ala): Allah made it lowest. As for the other, by its very nature and from the beginning, it is the highest. Therefore He did not say "and He made the word of Allah the highest," because it was never lowly so that Allah could make it high.

So: falsehood is something made, while truth is truth, established since Allah created it.

His saying: ﴿and for a specified term…﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 3] means: an appointed time, which is the Day of Resurrection. This creation was not created by Allah and left aimless; rather, it is for a limited term, which is the Resurrection, the day when this established universe will change, and all that is in it will be destroyed, and its structure will be dismantled brick by brick.

﴿On the day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens…﴾ [Ibrahim: 48]: the day the sun is folded up and the moon is lost, and all the means of living on earth are destroyed.

As for the Hereafter: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord…﴾ [al-Zumar: 69]. There is no sun or moon there. You, in this world, live by means and causes, while in the Hereafter you live by the Causer, glorified is He.

His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 3]: that is, they turn away. We have said that warning (indhar) is frightening from evil before its time, and it is a manifestation of Allah's mercy toward His servants, His kindness to them, and His eagerness for their salvation.

Whoever warns you of evil before you fall into it has done you a kindness. So among Allah's mercy to people is that He sent to them messengers as bearers of good news and warners, and revealed to them books and made the outcome clear to them. But what can be done with one who turns away from this warning and departs from it and pays it no heed?

Therefore, in Surat al-Rahman, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, made warning and intimidation one of the blessings of Allah that call for gratitude. He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and [molten] brass, and you will not be victorious. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 35-36].

So being frightened by these kinds of punishment is a blessing, because when you fear the consequence, you do not commit the act that leads to it. As they say in medicine: prevention is better than cure. Likewise, keeping away from disobedience is better than suffering its punishment.

The Exalted says, wanting to establish that those who have taken protectors other than Allah have taken them without any prior claim to perfection or any prior benefit they have conferred. So they took idols as gods to worship besides Allah, while they themselves fashioned them with their own hands...

Meaning of "And who is more astray..." (Al-Ahqaf: 5): It is a rhetorical question whose purpose is negation. That is: no one is more astray than the one who calls upon other than Allah those who do not respond to him, neither now, nor in the future, nor especially on the Day of Resurrection, while he knows that the god he calls upon does not respond to him.

Allah, glorified and exalted, is the One truly worthy of worship, the Great, the Most High. Therefore, when the disbeliever is touched by good, he does not resort to his false gods, and he never cries out, "O Hubal!" He does not say it in a time of hardship, because he knows that Hubal does not hear him and will not answer him. In this state he does not deceive himself or lie to himself, so you see him turning to Allah and calling upon Him, even though he disbelieves in Him.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him...﴾ (Al-Isra: 67). Yes, in the moment of distress he seeks the true God, the One who holds benefit and harm in His hand. He says, "O Lord!" But when Allah removes his harm, he returns to his disbelief and obstinacy.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us for a harm that touched him...﴾ (Yunus: 12).

Why? Because religion has become, for these people (Fanṭaẓiyya, i.e., Fantasia/the ones who believe in a "god" without a method), a belief in a god who has no law and no obligations. He did not say to them, "Do" and "Do not," so these were false gods even in name, because the god (ilah) is the one worshipped and obeyed in His command and prohibition. So all of this is falsehood and error.

When the Truth, glorified is He, clarifies this matter for us, He presented it in the form of this question so that we may answer, "And who is more astray...?" (Al-Ahqaf: 5), and we say, "No one is more astray than this," and that becomes an acknowledgment from them and a testimony to this.

As for His saying: ﴿And they are...﴾ (Al-Ahqaf: 5), i.e., the claimed deities, ﴿heedless of their call﴾ (Al-Ahqaf: 5), not aware of who is calling upon them.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 6:

﴿And when mankind are gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), they will be enemies to them (the deities)...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 6] That is: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿they will be...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 6] That is: the deities. ﴿...enemies to them...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 6] Yes, at this station the enmity among all of these becomes manifest, each one disowns the other, and some of them curse one another. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 67].

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, along with their companions and what they used to worship, besides Allah, and lead them to the path of Hellfire. And stop them, for they are to be questioned. What is the matter with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they will be submitting on that Day. And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another. They will say: "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right side." They will say: "Rather, you were not believers. And we had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people. So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us; indeed, we are to taste (the punishment). So we led you astray; indeed, we were ourselves astray." Indeed, they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment. Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾ [as-Saffat: 22-34].

This is a depiction of the dialogue that takes place among these wrongdoers and the blame and reproach that passes between them, where each one places the responsibility upon the other. Among this also is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved will say: "Our Lord, show us the ones who misled us from among the jinn and mankind; we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.﴾ [Fussilat: 29].

This is the argument of Satan on the Day of Resurrection. He says: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves...﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

We have said: the meaning of ﴿authority (sultan)...﴾ [Ibrahim: 22] is: proof. It is of two kinds: either a proof that persuades you to act, or a force that compels you to act. And I have neither this nor that. ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me...﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. From aṣ-ṣarkh: it means calling out and seeking aid. And aṣrakhahu means: he gave him aid.

So, on the Day of Resurrection, the enmity is clear between the wrongdoers and the disbelievers, between the worshipper and the worshipped, and their abode is all in the Fire: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98].

Some people raise an objection to this verse, saying: How can it be, when among them are those who worshipped Jesus, peace be upon him, besides Allah? How could Jesus be fuel for Hell? These people have overlooked that (ma) is used for non-rational beings, and it did not say (man).

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences...﴾.

The meaning of ﴿clear⁠﻿...﴾ is: manifest and evident. Yet ﴿those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them...﴾. They said about the truth, so the لام (lam) here carries the sense of (عن) ("about"). Or they went further: instead of confronting those who believed in the truth, they confronted the truth itself, and said: ﴿This is manifest magic﴾.

Refuting this claim is easy. We say to them: if we grant that it is magic, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) bewitched those who believed in him, then why did he not bewitch you as he bewitched them, and the matter would be settled?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 46, verse 8:

After they said that the Qur'an is sorcery, with which Muhammad bewitched his companions so that they believed in it, they said: "It is a fabrication (ifti'a') that Muhammad has fabricated," and ifti'a' is deliberate lying. So Allah answered them: ﴿Say...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8] Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿If I have fabricated it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8].

That is: you cannot ward off from me the punishment of Allah if I have fabricated against Him and lied in conveying His message. Therefore, He, glorified is He, says in another verse that clarifies this matter: ﴿And if he had invented about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta. And none of you could prevent Us from him.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44–47].

How then could the Messenger of Allah lie against Allah after this statement, when our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was known among his people as "the Truthful" even before his mission, because they had never tested him with a lie at all?

You know that from that day on, the testimony of Khuzaymah equals the testimony of two men.

This (nishan, a mark or sign) benefited the Muslims in the matter of collecting the Qur'an, for the compilers of the Qur'an would not write down a verse unless they found it recorded on the scraps (riqa', pieces of parchment), and two trustworthy witnesses (?udul) attested to its authenticity. Until they came to the end of Surat al-Tawbah and found a verse written down with only one witness, Khuzaymah, so they accepted his testimony alone, because his testimony equals the testimony of two men.

Consider the courtesy of dialogue even with the opponents of the Messenger of Allah and with those who openly accuse him of lying. He says to them: ﴿If I have fabricated it...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8], where "in" (if) expresses doubt, ﴿then you cannot avail me anything against Allah...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8], that is: you cannot ward off the punishment of Allah from me. ﴿He is most knowing of what you say therein...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8], that is, of what you abundantly speak and accuse with, and your claim that the Qur'an is fabricated.

﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8] The matter returns to Allah, and its affair is entrusted to Him, and He is content with His testimony between him and his adversaries. The testimony of Allah is the testimony of truth and the testimony of sincerity.

Therefore Allah bore witness to it for Himself, glorified is He, the testimony of the Essence to the Essence: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 18]. The angels also bore witness to it, a testimony of presence (mashhad), and those of knowledge bore witness to it by inference (istidlal): ﴿and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 18].

So, in this matter, the Messenger of Allah cannot produce a witness to his truthfulness in conveying the Qur'an from Allah, so he suffices with making Allah a witness between him and them.

This is from the courtesy of dialogue in which our master, the Messenger of Allah, was disciplined. They accuse him of deliberately lying while he is gentle toward them. In another place He responds to them, and the Truthful, glorified is He, says on the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit."﴾ [Hud: 35].

His saying at the end of the verse, ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8], is as if He is tender toward them and seeks to win their hearts: despite this false claim, the door of forgiveness and mercy remains open before you.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say, "I am not an innovation among the messengers..."﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 9:

﴿Say...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9] That is: say to them, O Muhammad, ﴿"I am not an innovation among the Messengers..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9]. Bid'(innovation, something new and originated that has no precedent) is the thing that is new and has no previous example.

Among its uses is the Exalted's saying: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion and He created all things, and He is Knower of all things?﴾ [al-An'am: 101]. That is: the Creator of them both without any previous model. We say: so-and-so is an innovator (mubdi'), meaning he has brought something that no one before him has reached.

The meaning is: "I have not come with a way other than that with which those Messengers before me came, nor am I an innovator of what I call you to. I am not the first Messenger to be met with denial and confronted with disbelief, obstinacy and persecution. Rather, all the Messengers before me have preceded me in that. They were harmed and denied, and they were patient until God gave them victory," as the Exalted said: ﴿So each one We seized for his sin...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40].

The custom of God regarding the earlier Messengers was that the heavens would take charge of disciplining those who denied the Messengers and opposed the call to truth. As for the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), God granted security to Muhammad and to his community that they themselves would take charge of disciplining the deniers of the call who clash with it, that they would support the truth, and that they would be worthy of it until the Hour arises.

Therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The good is intended for me in particular and for my community in general," such that each generation, or each one of them, takes a share of this excellence.

As for His saying: ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9], that is: "Now I do not know, but perhaps he will know in the future by what God reveals to him," as happened in the matter of fighting the disbelievers and proclaiming the call openly, when some of those who had embraced Islam with the Messenger of God asked to fight the disbelievers. He (ﷺ) used to say to them: "I have not been commanded, I have not been commanded."

When he (ﷺ) migrated to Medina, he agreed with them to fight. So: he proclaimed the religion of God openly in Mecca and did not wage war except in Medina, and there is wisdom in this. Mecca was the homeland of Quraysh and the seat of their dominance, and Quraysh was the object of attention and respect from all the tribes of the Arabs because of their status regarding the Sacred House of God and their service to its pilgrims.

Because Mecca lay on the trade route between Yemen and Syria during the journeys of winter and summer, it was necessary to observe this status of Quraysh and not to declare war on them at this time.

When we read, for example, Surah al-Fil: ﴿And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and made them like eaten straw﴾ [al-Fil: 3-5], if you ask "why?", Surah Quraysh answers you: ﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer﴾ [Quraysh: 1-2].

That is: God did this for the benefit of Quraysh, so that they would retain their status and awe among the tribes of the Arabs, and so that they would remain secure and at ease in their trade caravans between Yemen and Syria.

Therefore He said after it: ﴿Let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ [Quraysh: 3-4].

The meaning of ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9] is: "I do not know whether God will command us to fight these people, or will command us to leave Mecca for another place where we seek His support." Therefore after this the Messenger of God commanded them to emigrate to Abyssinia, and said: [...]. It was as if the Master, the Messenger of God, had a map of the world around him. Indeed, when they went to Abyssinia, the Negus honored them and protected them when Quraysh sent 'Amr in pursuit of them; so he rejected 'Amr and returned Quraysh's gifts, and believed in Muhammad and his call. Therefore the Messenger of God appointed him as his agent to marry him to Umm Habibah, and when the Negus died, the Messenger of God prayed over him (may God bless him).

The emigration to Abyssinia was a transitional stage in which the persecuted Muslims took refuge with this king under whom no one is wronged, until God permitted His Messenger to emigrate to Medina, where the support of Islam and the elevation of its word would come.

The wisdom is that the first proclamation of the call was in Mecca, while the support and strengthening of the religion came in Medina, because Quraysh were the masters of the Arabs and the holders of control in the Arabian Peninsula.

Had the support come in Mecca, they would have said it was due to the dominance and authority of Quraysh, which extended beyond the Peninsula to the world around it. So the wisdom was that the first proclamation of Islam should be in the ears of these masters, shaking them and denouncing their deeds, and nullifying their worship of idols.

But support was deferred until Medina, so that the religion would triumph through the Emigrants and the Helpers, lest someone suppose that partisanship for Muhammad is what created faith in Muhammad. Rather, faith in Muhammad is what created partisanship for Muhammad.

As for His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9], look here at the greatness in the personality of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He speaks with what is with him, as if he were saying: "If it is returned to me, I say: I am not like any of you; and if it is taken from me, I say: I am only a human being like you."

Thus: the Master, the Messenger of God, did not bring anything from himself except in matters where no ruling had been revealed. If he exercised independent judgment (ijtihad) in a matter where no ruling had been revealed and erred, God would correct him before he persisted, and he would not disdain that; and it is He who informs us of this correction, as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1].

Then the Truthful, Glorified One says:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if it is from God and you disbelieve in it...﴾.

...And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. This phrase resolved a difficulty for us and clarified the meaning of guidance (hidayah). For some say: If Allah has decreed disbelief upon the disbeliever and does not guide the wrongdoing people, then why does He punish them?

But this is a fallacy. Had the question been logical, it would have completed the picture by asking: Why does He reward the obedient when He has prescribed obedience for him?

We have already explained in this matter that Allah, exalted is He, guided all of them with the guidance of indication and direction (hidayat dalalah wa irshad). This category includes the believer and the disbeliever, and the obedient and the disobedient. Allah has indicated to all of them and made the straight path clear to them. So whoever takes hold of this guidance and walks by its light deserves more from Allah.

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. This type is the second kind of guidance, which is the guidance of assistance and enabling success (hidayat al-ma'unah wa al-tawfiq).

So His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means: He does not guide them with the guidance of assistance. Therefore He said concerning Thamud: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17]. That is: We guided them with the guidance of indication and direction, but they preferred blindness and misguidance and chose them over guidance, so Allah left them to what they had chosen, just as He assists the people of guidance in their guidance.

You remember the example we gave earlier to clarify this matter. We said: If you asked a traffic policeman, for instance, about the road, and he pointed it out to you, and you took his word and thanked him, he would increase you in direction, and perhaps he would even go with you until he brings you to your destination.

So then: The Exalted One does not guide the wrongdoing people because of their wrongdoing, nor does He guide the defiantly disobedient people because of their defiance, nor does He guide the disbelieving people because of their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 11:

The speakers here are those who disbelieved. To whom did they speak? To those who believed: ﴿Had it been good...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11], i.e., Islam, ﴿they would not have preceded us to it...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. The scholars have an observation on this verse that depends on the meaning of the phrase ﴿to those who believed...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11].

Whoever takes the particle (lam, "to") in its literal sense considers this statement a direct address from the disbelievers to the believers: they said to them, while they were present, "Had it been good, you would not have preceded us to it," with the second-person address (ta' al-khitab) in the verb. Whoever takes the lam to mean (ʿan, "about/concerning") understands it as referring to the believers in their absence from the gathering of the speech: "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it."

It is as if the context shifted from the particle (ʿan) to (lam) so as to give us both meanings: the meaning of harm in direct confrontation, and the meaning of harm in absence, combining them in a single text.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11] The ifk (falsehood) is the most vile of lies. ﴿Ancient (qadim)﴾ means: well known and established since antiquity, i.e., among the earlier generations.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 12:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And before it⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] i.e., before the Qur'an, ﴿was the Book of Musa⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] the Torah, ﴿a guide and a mercy⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] meaning: in its own time, and being a guide and exemplar by which they are guided, and leading to the mercy of whoever holds fast to it.

﴿And this⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a Book confirming⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] i.e., confirming the previous Books as they came from Allah, before they were altered or changed. In another place, Allah, glorified is He, explained that the Qur'an came confirming these Books and as a guardian over them all. ﴿In Arabic tongue⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] in the Arabic language, ﴿to warn those who have done wrong⁠—﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12] to frighten them about the consequence of their wrongdoing, ﴿and as good tidings for the doers of good﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12]. And "bushra" (good tidings) is the announcement of good before its time.

This verse has a parallel in Surat Fussilat: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast—the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

Yes, ﴿So there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13]. What fear could befall them, and what grief could descend upon them, when they uttered this word, ﴿"Our Lord is Allah..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13], which is the core of belief (lubb al-'aqidah)? And they did not utter it as an empty word; rather, they coupled it with action in accordance with this faith.

﴿Then they remained steadfast...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13], i.e., upon the commands and prohibitions of the creed. The meaning of istiqamah (steadfastness) is walking the straight path that the One you have believed in has laid out for you.

This steadfastness sets right the movement of your life and the movement of others with you. And steadfastness, in the terminology of engineering, is the shortest route that brings you to your goal.

Therefore we have said: guidance is a mount that carries you and brings you to your destination. Guidance is not a burden on its possessor; rather, you are the load upon it. The Exalted says: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord...﴾ [Luqman: 5]. So they ride upon guidance, and it carries them.

So then: whoever utters this word, ﴿"Our Lord is Allah..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13], and then remains steadfast upon it in the movement of his life, Allah guarantees him freedom from fear and freedom from grief, and He does not postpone this to the Hereafter; rather He makes it a glad tiding, which the angels give them, in the verse of Fussilat: ﴿the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

That is: they descend upon them at the moment of death, giving them good news and reassurance, so there is no fear upon them and they do not grieve. Fear is the anticipation of a matter that harms and injures, and grief is the calamity and pain of losing a beloved thing; they are secure from both of these. Since the matter is so, do not fear your enemies, for they will never gain anything from you.

Therefore they had a principle which they would declare to their enemies with courage: ﴿Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes? And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. So wait; indeed, we are with you waiting."﴾ [at-Tawbah: 52].

Meaning: if you confront us in battle, we await one of two matters: either we will defeat you, break your might, and humble you, or we will be killed and attain martyrdom. We are winners in either case, while you await that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. Thus the Muslims approached this matter with confidence and certainty unmixed with doubt.

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi on Surah 46, verse 14:

Allah's words: ﴿Those are…﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14] refer to those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast. The Truth tells us here of their reward and the outcome of their faith and steadfastness. They are ﴿the companions of Paradise…﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14], its companions. This may mean that they own it, or that it is a companion to them and they are companions to it. In other words, there is a bond between them of affection, understanding and inclination, each inclining toward the other and longing for it.

The companion (al-sahib) is the one whom you choose from among Allah's creation: one whose character matches your character, whose nature matches your nature, and whose conduct matches your conduct. Those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast, chose Paradise, and Paradise chose them, and it took them as companions and chosen friends.

It has been reported that Paradise longs for its people, awaits them and asks about them, just as the Fire longs for its people and awaits them. There is nothing strange in this, for every creature has a language through which it expresses itself, even inanimate things.

Allah says: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification…﴾ [al-Nur: 41]. Each glorifies in its own language, which you do not understand, because it does not speak your language. Rather, the One who created it gave it a particular language through which it communicates with its own kind.

The Qur'an tells us that an ant spoke with its fellow ants and they understood one another, and Sulayman heard its speech and thanked Allah for giving him the blessing of understanding these creatures. Therefore we have corrected the saying that "the pebbles glorified in the hand of the Messenger of Allah" (ﷺ). This is not a distinction, because pebbles naturally glorify; they glorify even in the hand of Abu Jahl. Rather, the correct statement is: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard the pebbles glorifying in his hand.

﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein…﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14], because the bliss of Paradise is lasting and eternal; it does not end, and it is not spoiled by what spoils the blessings of this world. What is yours will not escape you, and you will not escape it. ﴿As a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14]. It has been asked: is this reward a right owed to the servant, or is it a bounty from Allah?

They said: Paradise is a bounty from Allah, and deeds are merely a means (sabab) of entering it, not a price (thaman) paid for it. For when the Almighty and Exalted established laws (shara'i') for us, He established them for our benefit and our well-being, and for the proper ordering of our lives, both at the level of the individual and at the level of the community.

We reap the fruit of righteous deeds and find happiness in them in this world, and in addition Allah rewards us for them with the reward of the Hereafter, though nothing returns from it to Allah, and He does not benefit from it in any way. Therefore, entry into Paradise is an addition and a favour from Allah.

As for His words: ﴿for what they used to do﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14], there is a subtle point here: what is "deed" (al-'amal)? Deed is the limb (al-jarihah) acting for its task: the hand moves, the tongue speaks, the eye sees, and so on. But if you reflect on deed, you find that it has two parts: speech and action. The tongue takes one half of the deed by itself, and the other limbs take the other half. This is why it says ﴿they say﴾ and ﴿they do.﴾ And because speech conveys the method (al-manhaj) to which the limbs respond, in obedience or in disobedience.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 15 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man (goodness) toward his parents...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. We commanded him to do so and obligated him to it. The *wasiyya* (injunction, bequest) is that you ask the one you enjoin to do a good deed that benefits him in his life and his Hereafter, and helps him carry out his task. Therefore you find that most injunctions concerning important matters come at the end of life, as if the person is saying to his family and to those he enjoins: "Come, take from me the outcome of my experiences in life."

This root occurs in the Qur'an as *wassa* and *awsa*. *Wassa* indicates the repetition of the action, as in His saying: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man toward his parents...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], and in His saying: ﴿And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, and (so did) Jacob...﴾ [al-Baqara: 132]. As for *awsa*, it is causative (transitive), as in His saying, on the tongue of the Messiah, peace be upon him: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I remain alive﴾ [Maryam: 31]. It is like *anzala* and *nazzala*: *anzala* means once, while *nazzala* means successively.

The word ﴿al-insan (man)...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], which is the one enjoined, indicates absoluteness and generality, i.e., man in the absolute sense, from Adam until the Hour, as a generic noun, which in creation is contrasted with the word *jinn*. We say: *al-ins* and *al-jinn*. *Al-ins* means man, from *uns* (intimacy), i.e., some of us are intimate with one another.

As for the jinn, there is no intimacy between us and them, because we do not see them and we do not share their nature. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you cannot see them...﴾ [al-A'raf: 27].

So: this injunction is directed by the Truth, glorified is He, to people universally and to man in general. It therefore includes the believer and the disbeliever, the adult who is legally responsible and the child who is not. If he acts upon the injunction, he is rewarded for it; if he leaves it, he is not punished.

This matter can be compared to prayer. In the noble hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: So: the command is yours, and likewise the punishment is yours too, because he is still below the age of legal obligation.

Prayer at this age is training for him and habituation, so that he becomes accustomed to prayer and familiar with it from his childhood, and grows up upon it. Thus, when he reaches legal obligation, it is easy for him and familiar to him.

The word *al-walidayn* (the parents) means the father and the mother. They are the direct cause of existence. There is an indirect cause, which is the Supreme Existence that created Adam and Eve. That existence was from non-existence. As for our existence through procreation, it was from a cause, which is *al-walidan* (the two parents).

For the survival of the species and the cultivation of the earth, God, the Exalted, linked procreation—for a practical wisdom—to man's strongest instinct and his strongest pleasure. How? They said: when you look at a beautiful sight that your eye enjoys, or smell a pleasant fragrance that your nose enjoys. Likewise when you eat a dish you love.

So: every limb of yours has its own special pleasure. But the sexual act produces a pleasure and enjoyment that encompasses all the limbs, and all the limbs participate in it. Therefore God legislated the ritual bath (*ghusl*) after it, because all the limbs participate in this act, and also because during it you become heedless of God, and that required the ritual bath.

Also, because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, knew that children are a burden on their parents and a hardship in raising them, providing for them, and striving for them, God therefore swore by this matter, saying: ﴿By the begetter and what he begot﴾ [al-Balad: 3].

Were it not that God linked procreation to this pleasure, many people would perhaps renounce it. You see how much the woman suffers from the pains of pregnancy and childbirth, to the point that she says: "A repentance, I will never return," then she forgets her pains and hardships and yearns anew for pregnancy.

So: He linked procreation to this pleasure for a wisdom. But the strange thing is that people indulge in it, exaggerate, and take it beyond its limit, so that pleasure becomes the principle.

We see animals, for example, engage in it only for the survival of the species. Therefore, when the male comes to the female, he first smells her. If he finds her pregnant, he does not approach her, and she also does not allow him access to herself. And the strange thing is that we blame animals and say: "Bestial lust!" Glory be to God!

Furthermore, we notice in this matter that the childhood of man is approximately the longest childhood compared with the rest of creation. The animal, for example, gives birth, then the mother nurses her offspring, and after the period of nursing she no longer recognizes it and does not care for it.

As for man, he remains a child until the age of puberty. Read: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty...﴾ [al-Nur: 59]. That is because man is connected to, and bears a higher obligation from, the Truth, glorified is He, and is required to carry out His command and to refrain from His prohibition.

So: man's nature and his honoring through his connection with God made the period of his upbringing long, to suit his task in life. Look, for example, at a cow that gives birth: her calf falls, moves, shakes off the wetness from itself, then after minutes stands, then rises upright, then runs around her. All of this within an hour.

As for our child, he can sit after several months, for example, then crawls, then stands, then walks after a year or more. Indeed, among us there are those who extend the childhood of their children until the age of twenty-five, and he is treated as a child, supported and provided for, and not burdened with responsibility.

The injunction concerning parents occurs in the Qur'an in four places, joined with the worship of God: ﴿And worship God and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents...﴾ [al-Nisa': 36]. And He said: ﴿And when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except God, and (you shall show) kindness to parents...﴾ [al-Baqara: 83].

In Surat al-An'am: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and (show) kindness to parents...﴾ [al-An'am: 151]. And in Surat al-Isra': ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and (show) kindness to parents...﴾ [al-Isra': 23].

These are four places in which the Truth, glorified is He, commands the children to show kindness to their parents, and because of its importance He joins this with the worship of God, as if the two were equal in the balance. For the parents, as we have mentioned, are the direct cause of existence, and dutifulness toward them and kindness to them is a preparation and training that reminds you of the highest cause of your existence, who is the Creator, glorified and exalted is He.

This injunction God obligates upon us even if the parents are disbelievers, as we have said in the general injunction. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness toward his parents, but if they strive with you to associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 8].

And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman: 15]. So if God, the Exalted, enjoins us concerning parents even if they are polytheists, because they are the direct cause of existence, then what about the Supreme Cause of existence, glorified is He?

Some orientalists have objected here and said: The Qur'an says: ﴿do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman: 15], and in another verse it says: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their kindred...﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22].

They saw a contradiction between the two verses. This arises from failure to understand the language and lack of acquaintance with its styles and secrets. There is a difference between *wadd* (affection) and *ma'ruf* (kindness/good conduct). Affection originates in love and heartfelt emotion, whereas *ma'ruf* is a beauty that you produce toward the one you love and toward the one you dislike.

When the Truth, glorified is He, commands us to be dutiful to parents, it is only to give us training and discipline in being dutiful toward the one who created you and them, who is the Supreme Originator, glorified is He.

The word *ihsanan* (goodness) is the verbal noun of *ahsana*. In the sharia, *ihsan* is that you do good and kindness beyond what has been obligated upon you and of the same kind as what has been obligated upon you. God, the Exalted, explained this meaning to us in Surat al-Dhariyat: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good (muhsinin)﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 15-16].

Then He describes them and gives us the grounds of ihsan: ﴿They used to sleep but little at night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 17-19].

It is clear that these three matters mentioned are not obligatory upon the Muslim; rather, they are an addition of the same kind as what is obligatory upon him. Do you not see that He says concerning wealth: ﴿a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 19]? But when He speaks of the obligation of zakat, He says: ﴿a known right﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 24].

So the "known right" is the obligatory zakat, but "a right" in this unrestricted form refers to the charities that are given beyond the obligation. Whoever offers this extra in worship enters the domain of *ihsan*, which is the highest rank of worship.

Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, commands us to be dutiful to parents and to do good to them, because they have a favor upon us in bringing us into existence, in upbringing, and in providing for us. So we must give them more than they deserve, and when you give more than what is obligatory upon you, you are a doer of good to them.

So: the command regarding dutifulness to parents does not stop at the necessary obligation; it extends beyond it to the rank of *ihsan*.

Therefore, when the Truth, glorified is He, speaks to us about the right of parents, He says: ﴿So do not say to them, "Uff," and do not reproach them﴾ [al-Isra': 23]. *Uff* is a verb-like expression meaning "I am annoyed," and it indicates distress.

Beware of saying this word to them or showing impatience toward them, especially in their old age, when they are returned to the lowest point of life and are in the greatest need of tenderness and care.

At this age, a person returns to childhood once more: he needs someone to carry him, seat him, and feed him. Perhaps something may happen from him that causes harm, so beware of being hurt by him in this state.

Perhaps his legs tremble and he falls to the ground, or breaks a vase, for example. Beware of showing him anything that would hurt him. Know that you are rewarded for this, that it is stored up for you as a debt that will be repaid, and that whoever is dutiful to his parents, his children will be dutiful to him.

It is enough that when you are dutiful to him and bear his harm, you do so while wishing for his death, whereas he did more than this for you and wished you long life.

In light of this relationship between parents and children, we understand the hadith of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ): [the hadith text is incomplete in the original].

Early marriage, beyond being a protection for its possessor as well, is as the Arab said: "The nearest way to producing a father who will care for you in the childhood of your old age," for in this case the son attains the position of the father who cares for his child.

In another place the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness toward his parents...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 8]. There is a difference between *husn* (goodness) and *ihsan* (doing good). *Ihsan* is that you do a good deed toward them, whereas *husn* is the source of this action and the name of this process you carry out, as you say: "So-and-so is just (adil)," and "So-and-so is justice (adl)." That is, he has reached the ultimate in achieving justice, to the point that he and justice have become one thing.

So: *husn* is more eloquent than *ihsan*, and returning a favor with something better is an Islamic principle. Therefore He said: ﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it or return it﴾ [al-Nisa': 86].

The Truth, glorified is He, did not give the reason for: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness toward his parents...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 8].

Rather, after it He said: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 8]. That is: even in a situation of doctrinal opposition, He preserved this right for them, emphasized it, and enjoined dutifulness toward them in the best possible manner: ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 8]. And in the other verse He said: ﴿So do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman: 15].

They said: because fathers are of two types: a father who needs his son in order to live, and a father who does not need his son, meaning he is self-sufficient. Whoever is in need, you must accompany him with kindness, meaning you help him and establish his life in a dignified manner. Whoever is self-sufficient, he is on his own affairs, and the return of all is to God.

Here, in the verse before us, He mentioned neither *husnan* nor *ihsanan*. Rather, He mentioned the reason for the injunction, saying: ﴿His mother carried him in hardship and bore him in hardship, and his carrying and his weaning are thirty months...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. So here He specified the duration of pregnancy together with nursing in one statement, and in another verse He said about nursing alone: ﴿And his weaning is in two years...﴾ [Luqman: 14].

So: each verse took a snapshot, and by combining the two verses we can resolve some difficulties concerning the duration of pregnancy and the duration of nursing.

It was narrated that our master 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, entered upon our master 'Umar while there was a woman with him whom he wanted to punish with the hadd (prescribed punishment) for fornication, because she had given birth after six months while in her husband's house. The well-known view among them was that the duration of pregnancy is nine months.

'Ali said: "Take it easy, son of al-Khattab." Then he recited to him this verse: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning are thirty months...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], and said in the other verse: ﴿And his weaning is in two years...﴾ [Luqman: 14].

By subtracting the two years from the thirty months, it is permissible for the duration of pregnancy to be six months, which is the least possible period of pregnancy.

Therefore 'Umar said: "Evil is the place in a land where there is no Abu al-Hasan (i.e., 'Ali)." Indeed, 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was famous for knowledge and giving legal opinions (fatwa), because he entered Islam as a boy and drank from the spring of prophethood from his childhood, so his culture from its beginning was an Islamic culture. It is as if the cultural leaven in him from childhood was Islamic, whereas others had a pre-Islamic (jahili) culture.

And from the jurisprudence of Imam 'Ali and his mastery of the matters of the sharia: when the Messenger of God passed to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers) gathered at the Saqifa (the portico of Banu Sa'ida), and discussions took place between them, each wanting the caliphate after the Messenger of God. The Ansar aspired to it, and then they said: "From us a leader, and from you a leader."

When this reached our master 'Ali, he said: "You did not argue with them well. Say to them, that is, to the Ansar: 'Did you not hear the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)...'" So if leadership were among them, the (Prophet's) injunction concerning them would not have been made.

Among the amusing matters that occurred between 'Ali and 'Umar: 'Ali entered upon him and found him angry. He said: "What has angered you, Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "I asked Hudhayfa: 'How have you risen, Hudhayfa?' He said: 'I have risen loving sedition, hating the truth, praying without ablution, and I have in the earth what God does not have in the heavens.'"

'Ali laughed and said: "He has spoken the truth, Commander of the Faithful." He said: "Do you say it, Abu al-Hasan?" He said: "Yes." He means: he has risen loving his wealth and his children, and he recited: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15].

"Hating the truth" means death. And who among us loves it, Commander of the Faithful? "Praying without ablution" means: praying upon the Prophet (ﷺ). "And I have in the earth what God does not have in the heavens" means: he has a wife and a child. The strange thing is that in our time we hear someone belittling these figures, and even wanting to erase the personalities of Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Ali from our history.

Then we also note in this verse that the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿His mother carried him in hardship and bore him in hardship...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], meaning: unwillingly or with difficulty. And in the other verse: ﴿His mother carried him, weakness upon weakness...﴾ [Luqman: 14].

Al-Waahn, meaning weakness, results from pregnancy and childbirth. As for the dislike of this matter, it comes from the fact that women have different natures: some of them love this process, and some of them dislike it, but they obey their husbands while disliking it, and then they bear the hardships of pregnancy and nausea (al-wahm), then the pains of delivery. After childbirth, she occupies herself with the infant and tenderly cares for it.

Meanwhile, the father occupies himself with striving and seeking sustenance. Therefore, rationality predominates in the man and emotion in the woman, each according to his or her role in life.

Therefore, some err in understanding the saying of the Prophet ﷺ. When we reflect upon this hadith, we find that the crookedness of the rib is for its wisdom, because the ribs were created to protect the two most precious and important organs of the body, the heart and the lungs, and if the rib were straight it could not perform this task.

Would we say, for example, about the swallow (al-khattaf) that it is crooked, or that its crookedness is a defect in it? Certainly not, because the nature of its work and its function require that it be in this form. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ likened the woman to the rib, because her function is tenderness and compassion.

When Allah, glorified is He, enjoined us concerning parents, He mentioned the grounds of the injunction regarding the mother and did not mention anything of the grounds of the injunction regarding the father. They said: because the mother's role comes at a time when the child has no awareness by which he perceives his mother's role and her virtue during pregnancy, childbirth and nursing.

As for the father's role of providing and caring, it comes at a time when the child is aware of his father's kindness, understands his role in raising him and in managing his affairs. Therefore the child needs to be reminded of his mother's role and virtue, because he is not aware of it, whereas the father's role he already knows.

As long as we are discussing the role of parents in upbringing, we must mention the saying of the Almighty: ﴿And say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small."﴾ [al-Isra: 24]. This verse gives us the general methodology of upbringing for all children.

The two parents deserve this injunction for two reasons: they are the direct cause of existence, which reminds you of the Supreme Cause of existence, and they carry out upbringing, which reminds you of the Supreme Educator, glorified is He.

Allah is Lord and Educator: He created us from nothing and sustained us from non-existence, and He is the One who raised us and supplied us with the means of upbringing. Therefore, the injunction to be good to parents gives us training in goodness in our relationship with Allah, our Creator and Educator.

Then we also understand from this verse that upbringing alone is a cause and ground for goodness. A child may be raised by someone other than his parents, and the one who raised him has a favor over him that deserves goodness, because he carried out half of the process.

The father and mother have the favor of bringing into existence, and the educator has the favor of upbringing and has half the reward. This matter encourages sponsoring orphans and raising them seeking the Face of Allah.

Whoever loses his father, the whole society is his father. Therefore the Prophet ﷺ said: [...]. For if the father dies and leaves children, and they do not find from society anyone who looks after them and becomes a parent to them in place of their own parent, then when they do not find this, resentment arises in them towards the other children and resentment towards the whole society, and perhaps it extends to rebellion against Allah, who decreed orphanhood upon them.

The phrase ﴿as they brought me up when I was small﴾ [al-Isra: 24] means that upbringing has a time, which is the time of childhood. Therefore I recall that I was invited to deliver a lecture entitled:

"The Upbringing of Youth," at one of our universities. But before I began the lecture I said: I ask the honorable university director's permission to change the title of the lecture, because youth is not raised; youth is energy that is harnessed in the movement of life. Youth has already been raised.

If we said "the upbringing of youth," this title would be incorrect; rather, "the upbringing of childhood" or "of the young generation," because childhood is the dough that accepts shaping without objecting, whereas youth have already been shaped. Therefore they object, and they show impatience (tatnih) when you direct criticism or guidance at them.

But the youth at the university said: "We were raised wrongly, so re-raise us anew." I said to them: then re-live your childhood with us, and accept guidance and criticism without objecting. Be like the patient before the doctor, who accepts what he says without debate.

Among our errors in upbringing is that we prolong the period of childhood for our children. The family continues to embrace the son and spend on him until the age of twenty and twenty-five. Therefore the West has surpassed us in this matter: the boy, when he reaches puberty, becomes independent of his family and supports himself, even if his father is a millionaire.

Thereby the working hands multiply, unemployment decreases, and production increases, and these are all means of progress that we lack, and we have not yet been able to harness the energies of youth.

If you went to one of the capitals of the West, you would not see youth filling the streets and corners, nor would you find coffee-houses full of the unemployed. Rather, you see them at break time pouring out like locusts to take lunch. But the mistake they fell into is that they generalized this judgment to the boy and the girl.

The phrase ﴿رَبَّيَانِي..﴾ [al-Isra: 24] is in the dual and means the father and the mother. Each of them has a role in upbringing: the father brings in provision, and the woman manages and takes care of the affairs of her home.

Thus they are partners in this matter, and the presence of the woman in general in the home makes her influence stronger than the man's influence in the process of upbringing. Therefore, when we are concerned with gender-specific upbringing, we give the boy what suits him and give the girl what suits her.

It is therefore fitting for us now to mention the advice of the Arab mother to her daughter as she prepares her to move to the marital home. She says to her: "O daughter, if advice were to be left for lack of manners, it would have been left for you, but it is a reminder to the heedless and an aid to the intelligent.

O daughter, tomorrow you will leave the house in which you grew up and the nest in which you were raised for a house you are not accustomed to and a companion you do not know. So be a servant to him and he will be a slave to you.

O daughter: if a woman could do without a man because of her parents' wealth and her lack of need for others, you would be the most independent of people from him. But women were created for men, and men were created for them.

O daughter, memorize from me ten qualities that will be a treasure for you. As for the first and second: keeping company with him in contentment, good listening to him and obedience. As for the third and fourth: attention to the places of his eyes and nose, so that his eye never falls on anything ugly from you, and he never smells from you anything but the sweetest fragrance.

As for the fifth and sixth: attention to the time of his sleep and his food, for constant hunger is a fury, and disturbed sleep is anger. As for the seventh and eighth: guarding his wealth and being considerate toward his servants and his family.

The essence of the matter regarding wealth is good management, and regarding the family is good administration.

As for the ninth and tenth: do not disobey his command, and do not reveal his secret, for if you oppose his order you will embitter his heart, and if you disclose his secret you will not be safe from his treachery.

Then beware of rejoicing before him when he is worried, or of sorrow before him when he is joyful."

This is the advice of Umama bint al-Harith to her daughter Umm Unas bint Awf ibn Muhallim al-Shaybani. This advice was given before Islam, yet it contains such manners and counsel that if a wife acted upon it in our time she would resolve most of the family problems that fill the courts today.

If every mother raised her daughter upon these manners, our condition would be set right. But the reality is that we have abandoned these counsels and neglected to act upon them in our homes, and we have left the homes to the maids, and left upbringing to those other than its people, until we have become what we are.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. This is another stage of life, the stage of puberty. ﴿When he reaches his maturity⁠⁠⁠⁠...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] means: he reaches the limit in the completion of body, strength and mind.

Among this is His saying, exalted is He, concerning our master Yusuf: ﴿And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ [Yusuf: 22]. And He said concerning our master Musa: ﴿And when he reached his maturity and became perfect, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ [al-Qasas: 14].

So: reaching the age of maturity (ashudd), attaining full proportion, completion of body, physique and strength, and completion of mind, is the beginning of receiving wisdom and the beginning of legal responsibility (taklif). If he were charged before puberty, and then puberty and adolescence came with the changes they bring to the body, the servant might say: changes have come upon me that did not occur to me when I believed in You. Therefore, the process is deferred until the age of puberty, which is the peak of maturity.

The peak of maturity in a human being is that he becomes able to beget another like himself. Likewise in fruits, for example: we have said that a watermelon is not sweet to eat unless its flesh has ripened and turned dark, so that if you plant it, it gives you a new plant. When you eat this, you are assured the existence of others.

But if it is picked while its flesh is not yet ripe, you eat it, and then you plant the seed and it does not sprout. So here there is wisdom for the survival of the species.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening⁠⁠⁠⁠...﴾ [al-An'am: 99]. The word (yan'ihi, its ripening): you guarantee that you will bring a new tree. Also, you notice in fruit-bearing trees that if you do not pick the fruits, they fall by their own nature.

And from the wisdom of the Creator, glorified is He, and the wonders of creation: in the stage of growth and before puberty you find that the process of growth happens with precise, masterful calculation. Some things in the body grow and their counterparts in the body do not grow. Take for example hair, which grows and is cut from time to time, but the hair of the eyebrows and the eyelashes, for example, does not grow. Likewise, bones grow with the growth of the child until he reaches maturity, whereas teeth, which are also bones, stop at a particular shape and do not grow. Had they grown like the rest of the bones, they would have become like the tusk of an elephant.

So: the matter is not, as we have said, "mechanics," but rather "engineering" from the Originator of this universe, glorified is He.

﴿And reached forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. Because the age of forty is the age at which a person should stop, take account of himself, and correct his course.

The age of forty is the peak of mental maturity, and it is also the beginning of decline toward the end. Therefore Allah, glorified is He, draws our attention specifically to forty, so that we stop and make amends for what has passed.

The phrase ﴿awzi'ni..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] means: inspire me, help me, and strengthen me ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], beginning with the favor of bringing into existence, the favor of safety and well-being, the favor of Islam, the favor of success in obedience, and the favor that You made for me a father and a mother who undertook my upbringing.

Then he extends gratitude to the parents: ﴿and upon my parents..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], because a favor upon the father is a favor upon his child. ﴿And that I may do righteousness which You will accept..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], meaning: grant me success and help me to do righteous deeds.

Righteous deeds are steadfastness in carrying out the command and avoiding the prohibition in matters where there is a text. As for matters on which there is no text, you have the freedom to act or not to act.

﴿Which You will accept..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] means: that this deed be in accordance with the method You prescribed, or that You be pleased with it and accept it, or that You reward me for it.

﴿And make righteous for me my offspring..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] is a supplication that his goodness extend into his descendants, or it means: O Lord, I have been excessive toward myself and fallen short, and I do not want that for my offspring; I want for them the righteousness that was not achieved for me.

This is a well-known principle: a father wishes to make up in his children's lives what he missed in his own life, to realize in them the perfection he did not attain himself. Therefore a person is happy if his child surpasses him.

Consider the verb ﴿wa-aslih..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]: you find it transitive by itself, so why did he say (fi) and say ﴿wa-aslih li fi dhurriyyati..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] rather than "wa-aslih li dhurriyyati"? What is the necessity for this? The construction here is as if it made the offspring a vessel for the righteousness, and a person's vessel is his heart.

Therefore, it is related in the noble hadith: [...]. So he used (fi) to make them a container and a contained.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. Repentance is an open door until the end of one's life, but it should not be delayed, and we should not neglect it if we have been excessive toward ourselves. Yet some of us are taken by this world, which makes us forget ourselves, so we postpone repentance and reconciliation with our Lord until this age.

Therefore it is related in a narration, and in the meaning of another hadith, it is said: why? Because you took your ease in your youth and satisfied your desires of what you wanted. But when you reach forty, be ashamed to disobey Allah after it, and be ashamed to postpone repentance when you cannot guarantee your life after it.

The phrase ﴿And indeed, I am of the Muslims﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15] means: the deficiency or shortcoming was not in the belief, but in carrying out what the belief requires in the rulings.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 46, verse 16:

The word ﴿Those (ulā'ika)﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16] is a pointer to those previously mentioned and their attributes. ﴿Those from whom We accept the best of what they did﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. It is well known of the verb taqabbala (to accept) that it is transitive with min, as in the saying of our master Ibrahim: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il (said), "Our Lord, accept (taqabbal) from us"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 127].

In another place: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ [al-Shura: 25].

So it is transitive once with (min) and once with (ʿan), and each carries its own meaning. The saying of the Exalted, ﴿Those from whom We accept the best of what they did﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16], means: repentance bears from you the burden of sins and their weight, because it removes them away from you.

Therefore He said ﴿from them (ʿanhum)﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16], because the coming of one particle in place of another must have a wisdom, and that it adds a meaning which the other particle does not give. We already explained this matter in the saying of the Truthful, the Exalted: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has given me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq﴾ [Ibrahim: 39], where we saw that all the exegetes say: (ʿalā) here means: "with" old age.

Upon reflection on the verse, we find that (maʿa) is two letters and (ʿalā) is three letters. So why did the Qur'an turn away from (maʿa) and use (ʿalā)? How does it leave the easy two letters for the three?

When we reflect on the matter of the old age of our master Ibrahim, we find that the companionship which (maʿa) conveys is not sufficient. What is meant is a particle that gives a companionship in which the state is overcome, for old age was present with Ibrahim and accompanied him, but it was an old age overcome by the power of Allah.

It is as if the absolute power rose above the law of old age and broke the norm, so Isma'il came upon this old age. This meaning is not achieved by using (maʿa) but by (ʿalā).

Likewise in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing (ʿalā ẓulmihim), and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6]. It is as if sin calls for punishment, but the forgiveness of Allah rose above the punishment and overcame it. Therefore: when one particle is used in place of another, it must add a meaning which the first particle does not add.

Therefore: ﴿We accept from them the best of what they did﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16] means we bear from them the burden of what was before repentance. In another place the Exalted explains this meaning: ﴿Those—Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70]. So much so that one of them said: "By Allah, I regret that I did not commit the major sins, because Allah would have replaced them with good deeds." This is a mistake. For who knows whether you will live until you repent?

And His saying: ﴿and We overlook their evil deeds (wa-natajawazu ʿan sayyiʾatihim)﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16], that is, We pardon them and show forbearance ﴿among the companions of the Garden (fī ʾaṣḥāb al-janna)﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. We have said before: "companions of the Garden" means that between them and it there is companionship or friendship, or that its companions means its owners.

But here He says ﴿among the companions of the Garden﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. It is as if those we are speaking of are in the midst of the Garden, and the people of the Garden surround them, so they are at the center. This understanding comes from the meaning of (fī) here. But why did these deserve to be in the middle and at the center, with the people of the Garden around them?

They said: because one who became accustomed to sin and then turns to obedience finds it hard on himself, after having been drawn to sin and trained in it, so he struggles with himself to persist in obedience, unlike one who never experienced sin, for obedience is natural to him and needs no struggle as the former does. Therefore Allah treats them with this leniency and this grace, so He replaces their evil deeds with good deeds, and this is the utmost generosity.

Then the Exalted reassures them: ﴿the true promise which they were promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. It is as if they do not believe that Allah treats them with all this grace, so He reminds them that this is the promise of Allah, and the promise of Allah is a true promise that is never broken, and no one can annul or cancel this promise.

The Exalted gives His servants all these facilities and inducements: He accepts the repentance of those who repent, pardons those who do wrong, and replaces their evil deeds with good deeds, not only for the salvation of the penitent alone, but for the salvation of the whole society. For if repentance were not legislated, the society would be wretched through every sinner whose door of return was closed in his face, and evil would spread and prevail.

The Noble Qur'an gives us several snapshots of parents with their children, and these snapshots differ according to circumstances. Because of the importance of the relationship between parent and child, God linked the command concerning parents with His worship, and gave it the same importance and sanctity.

He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you show kindness to parents...﴾ [al-Isra: 23]. This is because the father and the child are the basic cell for building society. If this cell is sound, society is sound, and if it is corrupted, society is corrupted. The soundness of this cell requires us to know the status of the parents, and that they are the direct cause of our existence, so they have the right of causation in bringing us into being. That is, had it not been for them, the child would not have come to exist.

When we are dutiful to them and respect them, this is a training for us in magnifying and respecting the First Originator, glorified is He, and the original root of the matter.

Therefore this command came in general terms, without distinction between believer and disbeliever. The Truth enjoins good treatment of parents even if they are disbelievers, because He, exalted is He, is the Lord of all. He sustains all with life, provision and continuance, because the servant is His creation and His handiwork.

We have said: one must notice the difference between divinity (al-uluhiyyah) and lordship (al-rububiyyah). Lordship is giving and nurturing, while divinity is obligation and worship through obeying the command and avoiding the prohibition.

This too is a giving, but a giving of obligation: "do" and "do not do." It is a giving because its benefit returns to the servant, and God does not benefit from it at all. The obedience of the obedient does not add to Him any attribute He did not have, and the disobedience of the disobedient does not strip Him of any attribute that is His.

God possesses the attributes of absolute perfection before this creation came into being. Therefore we see that when a person is overwhelmed by a matter in his life that he cannot handle, he says: "O Lord (Rabb)!" So he calls upon Him by the attribute of lordship, meaning: O You who take charge of my care and nurturing, take my hand and help me.

But if he wishes to seek help in a matter of obligation from God, exalted is He, he says: "O Allah!" That is, O my God, O You who imposed obligations on me, help me to obey You in what You have imposed on me.

So: the wisdom of obligation does not return to God; it returns to the one who is obligated. The Truth, glorified is He, wants a believing, righteous society that builds and develops and is in the best condition, just as you urge your young child to study and say to him: "If you pass, I will buy you a bicycle or a suit." You want good for him, and you will not benefit from what you buy him.

Therefore it is recorded in the Hadith Qudsi: "So: the share of obligation is the well-being of the one obligated."

We have already clarified this matter in explaining His saying: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5]. Guidance is like a mount and a conveyance that carries the one who is guided and delivers him to the goal he strives for. Guidance is not a burden or a weight on its bearer; it is rather a helper to him.

The verse we have before us, ﴿And one who says to his parents, "Uff to you both..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], gives us a snapshot of parents when they are believers and the child is not a believer, and it depicts for us the parents' eagerness for the child's salvation, just as we saw, for example, in the story of our master Nuh and his son.

This verse was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr. His parents had embraced Islam, but he refused to embrace it. They used to call him to belief in God and belief in the Resurrection, and he would say to them: "Where is so-and-so? And where is so-and-so?" meaning those who had died among the earlier ones.

Then 'Abd al-Rahman embraced Islam afterwards and his Islam became good. There are narrations from Sayyida 'Aisha that she denied this and said: the verse was revealed concerning another person, and she mentioned his name.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And one who says to his parents...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17]: that is, remember the one who said to his parents ﴿Uff to you both...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17]. "Uff" (أفّ) is a verb-name in the present sense meaning "I am annoyed." They say: "So-and-so says uff" (yatafaffa). That is, he says "uff" and shows distress and annoyance at something filthy or foul-smelling, or at an act that does not please you.

His saying ﴿to you both﴾ indicates his anger at them, because they were pressing him.

So he said: ﴿Uff to you both...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], meaning: you two are not far from it.

But why does he say uff? They said: because the parents were insisting that he believe while he did not want to believe. When they pressed him too much, he expressed annoyance and said: ﴿Do you promise me that I will be brought forth...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17]. That is: that I will be resurrected after death. The interrogative hamzah here is for astonishment or denial, for he denies the resurrection.

Then he brings the proof that supports his point of view: ﴿The generations have passed away before me...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17]. That is: the generations passed on, and many died among those who came before, and I have not seen any one of them rise from his grave.

But whoever said that the resurrection would be in this world? The resurrection's appointed time is the Hereafter, after everyone has died and none remains but God.

But when the parents heard these words, and felt this determination upon disbelief, they found no rescuer except God, so they turned to Him: ﴿While they both call upon God for help, "Woe to you! Believe..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17].

This is a depiction of the nature of the parents and the intensity of their eagerness for the son's salvation. They are humbling themselves and pressing the son to believe, and to taste the sweetness of faith that they have tasted.

The phrase ﴿Woe to you! Believe...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17] is an urging on him to believe, or it means: woe to you if you do not believe. We note here that the verb "yastaghithu" (seek help) normally takes the preposition "bi" (with), so one says: "so-and-so seeks help with God." Why then is the preposition omitted and the verb made transitive by itself, saying ﴿they both call upon God for help (yastaghithani Allah)﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17]?

They said: this indicates that they are facing a difficult matter, and a hard, stubborn, obstinate heart that accepts no call and does not respond to the parents' appeal and does not appreciate their feelings.

So they turned directly to God that He guide this son, expand his breast, soften this hard disposition, so that he may listen, obey, and be saved. Therefore we said: you will not find anyone who wishes you good as your father does, who wants you to be better off than he is, and this is found only between parent and child.

So: in the face of this obstinacy, the parents have no recourse but to turn to God, the Turner of hearts and the Causer of causes. What the creatures' means cannot reach, leave to the Creator, glorified is He, for hearts are between two of His fingers; He turns them however He wills.
