Then, when he recognised his disobedience, he acknowledged it, repented of it, and confessed that he had wronged his Lord and wronged himself: ﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 23]. In al-Baqarah He said: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 37].

So, the repentance of Adam was accepted because he did not reject the ruling of God. As for Iblis, he rejected the ruling and did not submit to it, so he was expelled from the mercy of God and removed. There is a difference between disobeying a ruling while you acknowledge it and believe it is from God, and rejecting it.

Therefore we say these words to one who argues, for example, about matters of religion whose ruling is clear, such as usury (riba) or letting the beard grow. He says: "Dealing in usury is now permissible." We say to him: by this statement you reject the ruling of God concerning usury. The safer course for you is to say that it is forbidden, but my circumstances compel me to it, for example.

Then you may follow your father Adam and repent. Seek forgiveness, perhaps God will forgive you, rather than opposing your Lord in His ruling. You cannot bear this. And remember the words of Satan: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will change the creation of God...﴾ [al-Nisa': 119].

So beware of this matter. You know that Iblis was once, in his time, the "peacock of the angels" (Tawus al-Mala'ika). When he opposed, became arrogant, and rejected the ruling of God, He made him accursed and expelled from the mercy of God.

We have an important observation in God's command to Adam not to eat from the tree: ﴿And do not approach this tree...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]. The prohibition is against merely approaching it. And so it is with every command concerning what God has forbidden: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not approach them...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187].

As for what God has made lawful for you, He said concerning it: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229], meaning: do not transgress what God has made lawful. As for the forbidden, do not even approach it, because whoever grazes around the protected pasture is about to fall into it.

The offspring of Iblis follow his course in misleading the children of Adam. We do not see them, just as we do not see the angels, with the difference between them: the angels are made of light, and the devils are made of fire.

Here the discourse moves from the message of Muhammad ﷺ to mankind to the jinn, and the report that the jinn are under obligation and that they listen to the Qur'an. Muhammad ﷺ did not bring this from himself; rather he relates to us what God informed him, that the jinn listen to the Qur'an.

So He said in the surah of the Jinn: ﴿Say: "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said: Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to righteousness, so we have believed in it..."﴾ [al-Jinn: 1–2].

It is as if God, glorified is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad: I did not send you to go to the jinn and address them, because you do not see them. Therefore I turned them towards you and brought them to you so that they might listen to the Qur'an while you are unaware of them. Had I not informed you of that, you would not have known it.

Here He says: ﴿And [mention] when We turned to you a group of the jinn listening to the Qur'an...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29], so you recite while they listen around you.

Their words in the surah of the Jinn, ﴿which guides to righteousness...﴾ [al-Jinn: 2], and here they said: ﴿a Book revealed after Moses...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], indicate that the jinn have a connection with the earlier prophets, and that they are under obligation like us.

In the surah of al-Rahman: ﴿We will soon attend to you, O two weighty ones﴾ [al-Rahman: 31], meaning: We will take account of you. After We left you at your ease to do what you wish, do not think that this is heedlessness on Our part concerning you. Rather, We gave you respite in order to affirm the matter of choice which We created in you and granted you.

So the two weighty creations, the jinn and mankind, are equal in reckoning, just as they are equal in obligation.

It was narrated from our master Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of the mountains of Makkah, when there came toward us an old man with a staff he leaned upon. When the Messenger saw him, he recognised him, and said: "It is as if this is the gait of a jinni," and he composed (verses). The man said: "Yes, I am from the jinn." The Messenger said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Hamah ibn Haym ibn Laqis ibn Iblis." He said to him: "Between you and your father Iblis are there two fathers?" He said: "Yes, and I have lived most of the age and a little remains. And I witnessed Qabil while he was killing Habil."

This report is evidence of the length of their lifespans and that they take on different forms, just as the angel does. We do not see the angel in his true form, nor do we see the jinni in his true form, except when he takes the form of a human being.

You know the long hadith of Gabriel. Therefore we see some enemies of the Muhammadan call raising certain difficulties around it, among them their saying that the Messenger should be an angel. This difficulty is rejected: if the Messenger had come as an angel, he would have come to them in the form of a man; otherwise, how would he convey to them, and how would the receiving from him take place?

So the difficulty remains. Moreover, an angel cannot be a valid model, because they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded. How could he be a model for one whose nature is error, heedlessness, and forgetfulness?

Therefore a condition for the prophet and messenger is that he be of the same kind as those to whom he is sent, so that the model may be realised in him.

God, glorified is He, has given us a detailed picture of the state of the jinn, that among them are believers and disbelievers. He said, relating about them: ﴿And among us are the Muslims, and among us are the deviators. Whoever embraces Islam, those have sought out the right course. But as for the deviators, they will be fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Jinn: 14–15].

Therefore the Prophet ﷺ said: [...], so to You is praise, they repeat it according to the repetition of the verse.

Listen to them saying: ﴿And that He, exalted is the majesty of our Lord...﴾ [al-Jinn: 3], meaning: His majesty is exalted, and because of this majesty ﴿He has not taken a companion or a son﴾ [al-Jinn: 3]. So the jinn know the matters of faith and the matters of tawhid, and perhaps they were more precise than us in expressing them. It is enough that they judged Iblis to be foolish, saying: ﴿And that our foolish one used to say about Allah an excessive transgression﴾ [al-Jinn: 4].

Let us return to what we were discussing from His saying: ﴿And [mention] when We turned to you a group of the jinn listening to the Qur'an...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]. The nafar are the group from three to forty. "We turned them to you" means: We brought them to you instead of you going to them.

﴿So when they attended it...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]: they attended the recitation. ﴿They said: "Listen attentively"...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]: they listened with attention and reflection, meaning some of them instructed others to listen silently. ﴿So when it was concluded...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]: the recitation ended. ﴿They turned back to their people as warners﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]: they went to their people to warn them and convey to them what they had heard.

﴿They said: "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], that is, the Qur'an. Their saying "after Moses" indicates that they had a connection with the earlier messengers, and that they were believers in our master Moses, meaning they were from the Jews.

They mentioned Moses without Jesus, peace be upon them both, because the Book of Moses is the method that organises the movement of life, and in it are laws and rulings, whereas the Book of Jesus was merely matters of feeling and admonitions. Therefore they paid attention to this matter and combined the Gospel and the Torah in one book, despite the partisanship between them, and they named it the Holy Book.

The meaning of ﴿confirming...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30] is that the Qur'an confirms ﴿what is before it...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], the heavenly books that came before it. And since it confirms them, it came with what they came with, but it adds to them that it ﴿guides to the truth and to a straight path﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], in a manner suited to the universality of religion.

Every messenger before Muhammad came to treat the diseases of his society in a limited time and a limited place. Two messengers might be contemporaries, as we saw with our master Abraham: our master Lot was his contemporary, and our master Moses was contemporary with our master Shu'ayb.

The world at that time was in isolation and separation. There was not the connection that exists now, which makes the whole world like a small village. This isolated life made every society unaware of others.

Therefore each had its own particular corruptions, each of which needed a messenger to correct it and to take the hand of his people to God. Some people worshipped idols besides God, others cheated in measure and weight, and others deviated sexually from the nature God had created. Each of these groups needed a messenger.

But when the world became connected and means of travel came into existence, one messenger was necessary, because the corruptions and horizons would become unified. There had to be one messenger suitable for every time and every place. Therefore every time and every place was honoured by the one who gathers all good in every time and every place: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ﷺ.

So among the jinn there was a group who listened and undertook the duty of conveying the message. Therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes. And who knows, perhaps the one who conveys may be more eager to apply it than the one who hears." The Arab poet was alert to this meaning and said:

So take from my knowledge and do not look at my deeds,
and pick the fruit and leave the branch to the fire.

Then this group of jinn continue to convey to their people and warn them with what they heard:

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah...﴾.

The meaning of ﴿the caller of Allah﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31] originally refers to the Messenger of Allah, and then to the one who conveys on his behalf the method of Allah to the people. ﴿And believe in him﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31], i.e., in what he brought. ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]. He said ﴿of your sins﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31], so "min" (from) conveys partiality. That is: He will forgive you some of your sins, and this forgiveness is the fruit of faith.

He did not say "all the sins," because the Truthful, glorified is He, forgives some of them and leaves some for repentance and turning back to Him. For example, among sins are those that are expiated by prayer to prayer, or Friday to Friday, or Ramadan to Ramadan.

But there are sins that cannot be forgiven without repentance, and their forgiveness has other conditions, such as when they are against the rights of people. There are also wrongs and obligations that must be returned to their owners. ﴿And protect you from a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]. So: sins give rise to punishment in the Fire, and when He forgives sins, He protects their owner from the Fire. This is the principle of "takhliyah before tahliyah" (clearing away before adorning), as we mentioned.

However, it does not say here that they enter Paradise, and this raises a question for us: Does the jinn who believes enter Paradise? Some hold that after the reckoning they will turn to dust and the matter ends, based on the fact that it is not said here that they enter Paradise after He protects them from the Fire.

But since they are accountable like us, among them believers and disbelievers, then there must be recompense with Paradise or with the Fire. If you stop at the matter that they were created from fire, how are they punished by it? This is a remote matter in our minds, but it is easy for the Creator, glorified is He, for He has other laws.

We have said before: you are created from clay, so does that mean that if you go down into the sea, for example, (you are scorched)? Then recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire﴾ [as-Saffat: 64]. How does a tree grow at the root of Hellfire? So: do not speak about this matter, and Allah knows best about His creation.

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he cannot escape [Allah] within the earth...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32]. "Mu'jiz" means: one who causes others to be unable. "Ajz" is a weakness that prevents you from acting. You say: So-and-so made so-and-so incapable, i.e., he caused him what he cannot accomplish. From this is our saying: the Qur'an is "mu'jiz," meaning it rendered the Arabs unable to produce its like.

Those who disobeyed the caller to Allah and disbelieved in Him will not render us powerless, and they will not find any refuge from our punishment nor any escape from it.

﴿And they have no protectors other than Him﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], i.e., they will not have those who support them or defend them or intercede for them, and no power will prevent the punishment of Allah from them. ﴿Those are in manifest error﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], i.e., these supposed protectors have strayed from them, lost, so they have no existence.

"Mubin" [manifest] means encompassing, like the lost one who has lost his way, who goes here and goes there, not guided to the goal he desires.

Then the context returns, drawing their attention to the cosmic signs, perhaps they will reflect upon them, for they denied and rejected and did not benefit from the means of perception Allah placed in them, such as hearing, sight, and reasoning. The discussion returns once more to the cosmic signs and presenting them to them as a way of varying the admonitions.

The Most High here mentions one of the greatest of the signs of creation, which is ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 33]. Therefore He said in another place: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind..﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

He mentioned the creation of the heavens and the earth and did not mention the creation of man, because it is the greater sign. And where is the lifespan of a human being, who lives for a number of years, or even a hundred years, compared with the age of the heavens and the earth?

﴿And He was not wearied by their creation..﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 33]. He, the Exalted, did not tire, far exalted is Allah above that, as He said in another verse: ﴿And no fatigue touched Us.﴾ [Qaf: 38]. So whoever has these attributes, and these are the signs of His creation, is He not able to bring the dead back to life?

The answer comes: "Bala" (بلى), meaning: yes, He is able. The word "bala" (بلى) is used here to affirm, because the question is a negative question, and the rule is that the negation of a negation is an affirmation. ﴿Indeed, He is Able over all things.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 33] This is a concluding statement (tadhyil) that affirms Allah's power, not only over the reviving of the dead, but His power, the Most High, over all things.

This is another glimpse of the matter of being presented before the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah. Before this, He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them..."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20]. So He mentioned to them the reason for their being exposed to the Fire, which is that they used up all the good things in this world, such that nothing remained for them in the Hereafter.

Therefore we have said: the blessing that preoccupies its possessor from the Bestower is in reality a curse and a calamity upon him. The true blessing is the one that reminds you of the Bestower. For this reason our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), taught us that when we see a blessing with us or with others, we should say: "Mā shā' Allāh, lā quwwata illā billāh" (What Allah wills; there is no power except with Allah).

For you return the favour to its owner, and you clear yourself of conceit and of attributing the blessing to yourself, claiming it came through your own skill and cleverness, as Qarun did when he said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess﴾ [al-Qasas: 78].

The outcome was: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ [al-Qasas: 81]. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, were saying to him: since you were given it on account of knowledge with you, then guard it with knowledge from Us as well.

We have also mentioned the saying of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "By Allah, if I wished to be the best of you in food and the finest of you in clothing, I could have done so, but I hold back." Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Eat and drink with wholesome enjoyment for what you sent forward in the days past﴾ [al-Haqqah: 24].

So: whoever recalls the reward and keeps the bliss of the Hereafter in mind, the hardship of obedience in this world becomes light for him, like the student who studies, stays up late, and deprives himself of the pleasure of rest, longing for a greater pleasure, which is the pleasure of success.

His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And the Day when they are exposed...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 34]: the address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "Yawm" (Day) is an adverbial of time, meaning: mention the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, and remind them of it. And say to them: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 34], i.e., the truth that you used to deny has now become a reality.

We have already explained that knowledge has three stages: ʿilm al-yaqīn (knowledge of certainty), ʿayn al-yaqīn (eye-witnessed certainty), and ḥaqq al-yaqīn (truth of certainty). Reporting about the Hereafter and what it contains of reward and punishment is ʿilm al-yaqīn; then, when we see this recompense, it becomes ʿayn al-yaqīn; then, when we experience it and the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, it becomes ḥaqq al-yaqīn.

These stages are mentioned in two places in His saying: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you, until you visit the graves. No! You will come to know. Again, no! You will come to know. No! If you knew with certainty of knowledge, you would surely see the Hellfire; then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty; then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ [at-Takathur: 1-8].

As for ḥaqq al-yaqīn, it is mentioned in His saying: ﴿But if he was among the deniers, the astray, then for him is a welcome of boiling water, and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the true certainty. So exalt the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 92-96].

His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes, by our Lord"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 34] is their answer to the question ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 34]. The answer with "Balā" here means "yes," because the negation of a negation is an affirmation. Yes, this is the truth that we used to deny. It is not enough for them to acknowledge it; they also swear oaths to emphasize the matter.

﴿Yes, by our Lord﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 34], because they have witnessed it and experienced it. Then comes the final judgment: ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 34], i.e., because of your disbelief.

The address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah, glorified is He, consoles him and steadies him so that he may bear the harm inflicted by the disbelievers. He is not unique in this, for many of his brother messengers preceded him, so let Muhammad be patient as they were patient.

You know that our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was subjected to much harm from his people. They harmed him with words, saying: "Sorcerer, poet, madman, soothsayer, and liar." Then the harm went beyond words to deeds: they attacked him at Ta'if until his feet bled, his front tooth (rubā'iyyah) was broken at Uhud, and they threw the entrails of a camel on his back while he was praying.

They harmed him in his person, harmed his family and those who believed with him, and even plotted to kill him, and they constricted him until they forced him to leave Makkah for Madinah. The Prophet (ﷺ) bore all of that, but he was human, and such things weighed upon him.

So Allah, glorified is He, wished to set before him an example and a model of those messengers who were patient: ﴿So be patient, as the messengers of firm resolve were patient...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

Our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) reached the point of being thrown into the fire, yet the situation did not cause him to lose his trust in his Lord. The proof is that when Jibril (peace be upon him) offered to put out this fire, he said: "As for you, no." Then the command came from the heavens: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69].

In his youth he was tested in his person, and in his old age he was tested with the sacrifice of his only son. He was patient under the trial, so Allah ransomed the one to be sacrificed, Isma'il, and gave him in addition another son, our master Ishaq, and after him our master Ya'qub, and all of them were prophets.

This bounty came as a result of submission to Allah in His decree and His destiny, and contentment with it. For us, in the father of the prophets there is a model of contentment with the decree, and we should raise our generations upon that, because submission and contentment with Allah's decree are the first of the causes for the lifting of affliction. A affliction is not lifted until its bearer is content with it; otherwise the calamity remains descending upon him.

Those upon whom Allah's decree lingers long are themselves the cause of that, because in reality they are objecting, and had they been content, Allah would have lifted it from them. It is like the father who beats his son for a mistake he committed: if the son submits and yields to his father, the father leaves him, and even inclines toward him and pleases him. But if he objects, he beats him more.

So: Allah, exalted is He, wants to train His servant through trial. Therefore a hadith qudsi has come: ...

Consider the trials that our master Yusuf passed through: in his youth he was thrown into the well and sold as a slave, and in his adulthood he was tested with the wife of the ruler (al-'Aziz) and was thrown into prison. But he was patient, so Allah established him: ﴿And thus We established Yusuf in the land, to settle in it wherever he wished. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will...﴾ [Yusuf: 56].

We have previously explained that decrees are never devoid of wisdom, and that an event is not separate from its doer, so before you object, look at who the doer is. When the Prophet (ﷺ) reflects on the processions of his brother messengers before him and what they were exposed to, the harm from his people becomes easier for him to bear, and that serves as consolation for him.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35], it means: do not hasten their punishment, especially since they used to seek hastening of punishment out of ignorance and obstinacy. Therefore his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will return﴾ [Ghafir: 77], meaning: if you die, O Muhammad, before you see Allah's vengeance upon them, then their appointment is the Hereafter.

As for His saying: ﴿As if, on the day they see what they are promised...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35], it means: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will not have remained except an hour of a day...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35], meaning: the stage of the barzakh passes as though it were an hour of a day. Since the time of our master Adam until the Hour is established, he will not perceive this time, and it is to him merely an hour of a day, because time, as we have said, is a consequence of an event; if no event exists, time does not exist, as with a sleeper, for example.

We saw this in the story of the People of the Cave: Allah cast sleep upon them and they slept ﴿three hundred years and added nine﴾ [al-Kahf: 25], yet when they rose they said: ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day...﴾ [al-Kahf: 19], because of the absence of events that make one aware of time. So: do not hasten the punishment for them, for it is merely an hour, however long the time may be.

And you know the story of 'Uzayr: ﴿Or like the one who passed by a town while it was fallen upon its roofs. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 259].

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿A notification...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35]. Balagh (notification/conveyance) means reaching the goal. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿This is a notification for mankind, that they may be warned by it...﴾ [Ibrahim: 52], meaning: the limit of what I can admonish you with.

Since He, glorified is He, has said "this", it is necessary that it will happen, and nothing can prevent it, for He is one God with no partner and no opponent: ﴿Will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

Fisq (defiant disobedience): departing from obedience, and it is the cause of destruction in the Hereafter, or even in this world.
